name: dsh-vscode
description: Run the DeepSeek Harness agent inside VS Code. The extension manages a local dsh backend and embeds the full Harness Web UI.

dsh.backend.command.markdownDescription: Executable used to launch the backend. Defaults to `dsh` (must be on PATH). `${workspaceFolder}` is expanded to the first workspace folder. When developing inside the deepseek-harness monorepo, set this to `node` and use `#dsh.backend.args#` to point at the workspace CLI.

dsh.backend.args.markdownDescription: Arguments passed to `#dsh.backend.command#`. Must launch the Harness web server (the `web` subcommand). Each flag and value should be its own array item (`["--import", "tsx/esm", "…/bin.ts", "web"]`). A single item that starts with `-` and contains spaces is split. `--no-open`, `--host 127.0.0.1`, and `--port <port>` are appended automatically when not already present. `${workspaceFolder}` is expanded in each argument.

dsh.backend.port.markdownDescription: Port for the backend web server. `0` picks a free port automatically.

dsh.backend.autoStart.description: Start the backend automatically when the extension activates.

dsh.backend.cwd.markdownDescription: Working directory for the backend process. Empty uses the first open workspace folder, so the in-app directory picker starts there. `${workspaceFolder}` is expanded.

dsh.backend.readyTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long to wait for the backend to print its `dsh web:` URL or accept HTTP on the bound loopback port before reporting a start failure. Increase this for a slow source (`tsx`) launch.

dsh.backend.env.markdownDescription: Extra environment variables for the backend process (for example `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`). The API key is normally entered in the embedded Models page instead.
